Scenario 1-Minimum Development for Shipment via Rail - This scenario conforms with the minimum production requirements of the amended leases with the Crow Tribe and should be viewed as the most probable development level. Maximum production on Tract III would be reached in 1989 when 15 million tons/year would be produced with 3 draglines. Maximum production on Tract II would require 1 dragline with maximum production of 4 million tons/year reached in 1982. Combined production would reach a maximum of 19 million tons per year by 1989.
Scenario 2-High Development for Shipment via Rail - This scenario assumes that all coal within both tracts is or will be economically recoverable. A maximum of four draglines would be required on Tract III and two draglines on Tract II. Maximum production on Tract III would be achieved in 1992 with 18 million tons/year and on Tract II in 1990 with 8 million tons/year. Maximum production would reach 26 million tons per year by 1992.
Scenario 3-Energy Conversion - It is assumed that 6.5 million tons of coal would be required annually, and that one dragline would be necessary. The low development scenario for Tract II is combined with the above described assumptions for Tract III. Maximum coal mined would reach 20.5 million tons by 1985.
Although this conversion scenario is considered to have a very low probability of occurring, the potential impacts related to employment are of such magnitude that it merits serious if not detailed assessment.
